subject: Bridging charge proposal & capacity growth commitment
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chou <amy.chou@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridging charge proposal & capacity growth commitment

Hi Amy —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. We dug into Elara's Q1 token/hour profile and saw a concentrated two-week spike that pushed usage materially above the committed capacity in your current term. To avoid service interruption and to keep the environment stable while you finalize the longer-term commit, we propose the following: 

- One-time bridging charge of $32,400 to cover the excess inference hours between 2027-01-15 and 2027-02-01 (details in attached usage_report_Q1-2027.csv)
- In exchange, Redwood will apply a 25% credit on that charge towards the first month of the expanded commitment if Elara signs a capacity uplift of at least +30% for the next 12-month term (SOW amendment attached)
- We can issue a single invoice for the bridging charge (net 30) and provide the credit as a line-item reduction on the first renewal invoice after the new term begins

Attachments: usage_report_Q1-2027.csv, bridging_charge_calc.xlsx, SOW_Amendment_Elara_v1.pdf

Next steps: if this approach looks acceptable I can route the SOW amendment for signature via DocuSign and have Finance generate the bridging invoice in the next 24 business hours. If procurement needs a PO number up front, let me know the PO and we’ll attach it to the invoice.

Open to alternate structures if your team prefers crediting as prepaid capacity or amortizing across two months — happy to discuss.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0121

---
Note: See attached spreadsheet for line-by-line calculation; Ben and Monica are copied for accounting alignment.

Sergio —

Appreciate the write-up and the transparency on the spike. A couple quick questions before I take this to procurement: 

1) Can you show the hourly breakdown for the spike window and confirm that there were no anomalous retries or replays on our side that inflated token counts? (we'll double-check but would appreciate the callouts)
2) If we sign the +30% uplift, does the 25% credit apply immediately against the bridging charge or only after the new term starts? Our accounting prefers credits applied at invoice time rather than retroactive line-item credits.

Also include our AP contact if you need a PO: elara.ap@elarahealth.com.

Thanks — I’ll loop in procurement and get back with a PO request if the math checks out.

—Amy

Amy —

Quick answers from an accounting/ops perspective: we validated the raw logs and the spike maps to customer traffic (no system-side replays). The attached bridging_charge_calc.xlsx shows the per-hour reconciliation and how we arrived at $32,400 (excludes credits and taxes).

On credits/timing: we can apply the 25% credit in one of two ways (pick which works best for Elara):

A) Apply as an immediate credit against the bridging invoice (reduces the one-time invoice amount) once the SOW amendment is fully executed (preferred for simplicity)
B) Apply as a line-item credit on the first invoice after the new term begins (if your AP requires credits to be itemized on renewal invoices)

Either way we will not process the invoice until we have either a signed SOW amendment or a PO number that commits to the +30% uplift. If you need a smaller phased uplift we can structure a pro-rated credit — e.g., +15% uplift -> 12.5% credit.

I’ve asked Monica to scope the DocuSign envelope and the billing flow.

Ben Carter
